adversarial_critique: Claude's stored effect-size estimates (+27.2% consumption, +0.35 SD cleanliness, OR = 2.16 perceived ease and OR = 2.76 affordability for own BWD connection; -20.8% consumption and OR = 2.71 affordability for shared/other connection), upfront cost figures (PHP 10,000-14,000 / US$234-327) and survey sample size (N = 396) match Mason (2014, Table 2 and PDF pp. 13-15, 18 / pp. 500-502, 505) verbatim, although the dossier omits the printed standard errors (0.07, 0.13, 0.26 and 0.42 in Table 2) and cites a non-existent Table 4/5 in a paper containing only Table 1 and Table 2. For the extracted contrast (BWD connection = Household vs. None), all four regression coefficients are positive and statistically significant (p < .01 to p < .05) and outcome_polarity = "higher = better" holds across all four outcomes because Affordability was explicitly coded 1 = water expenses of 10.0% or less of household income (PDF pp. 9, 14 / pp. 496, 501). However, coding S882 unconditionally as Favourable in Family A (with alternative_substantive_direction left blank) depends on a contestable construct selection: in the exact same Table 2 models (PDF pp. 13, 16 / pp. 500, 503), formal housing tenure (Homeownership, 1 = yes vs. 0 = no) is statistically null across all four water-security outcomes (Est. = 0.09, 0.20, -0.07 [OR 0.94] and -0.26 [OR 0.77], all p >= .05), while the co-modeled Shared/other way BWD connection category (31.1% of households) exhibits a significant 20.8% decrease in consumption (Est. = -0.23, SE = 0.07, p < .001), null cleanliness (0.18, SE = 0.14) and null ease (0.41, SE = 0.27) alongside higher affordability (OR = 2.71, p < .05). Furthermore, exposure_full conflates cross-sectional possession of physical piped infrastructure (classified by the author as a household physical resource, p. 496) with the institutional barrier required to obtain it (the PHP 10,000-14,000 connection fee and piping cost), even though the qualitative component (n = 18, PDF pp. 18-19, 21 / pp. 505-506, 508) demonstrates that high upfront fees, restrictive case-by-case installment terms (PHP 3,000 down plus PHP 3,000 over 3 months), slow application processing and informal "under the table" payments operate in the opposite (Unfavourable) direction by excluding low-income households from connecting. Because Favourable accurately reflects the primary association of holding an own metered connection relative to relying on unpiped sources, whereas Null (via Homeownership), Mixed (incorporating Shared/other BWD connections) or Unfavourable (orienting around the connection-fee and administrative barrier) are equally defensible Family A synthesis choices from the same paper, the substantive direction is defensible_both_ways.

numerical_check_note: All six stored numerical estimates (+27.2% consumption [Est. = 0.24, SE = 0.07, p < .01], +0.35 SD perceived cleanliness [Est. = 0.35, SE = 0.13, p < .01], OR = 2.16 perceived ease [Est. = 0.77, SE = 0.26, p < .01] and OR = 2.76 affordability [Est. = 1.01, SE = 0.42, p < .05] for own household BWD connection; -20.8% consumption [Est. = -0.23, SE = 0.07, p < .001] and OR = 2.71 affordability [Est. = 1.00, SE = 0.44, p < .05] for shared/other BWD connection), upfront connection costs (PHP 10,000-14,000 / US$234-327) and survey sample size (N = 396) match Table 2 and the text verbatim (PDF pp. 13-15, 18). However, the dossier's effect_sizes.csv entry records CI/SE as "none, none / none" despite standard errors being explicitly printed in Table 2 (PDF p. 13), and misstates the provenance location as "Table 4/5" whereas the paper has only Table 1 and Table 2.
polarity_or_orientation_issue: Outcome polarity ("higher = better") is valid across all four outcomes, including Affordability, because the author dichotomized monthly water expenses as 1 = 10.0% or less of household income vs. 0 = greater than 10.0% (PDF pp. 9, 14). However, exposure orientation in Family A is contestable: Table 2 orients the variable around already possessing an own physical BWD connection vs. none (positively associated with water security, partly reflecting wealth selection into cheaper piped water vs. tanker/jug water at 4x-11x BWD prices), whereas exposure_full invokes the upfront PHP 10,000-14,000 connection and piping cost, which in the qualitative analysis (PDF pp. 18-19, 21) acts alongside restrictive installment plans and informal payments as an exclusionary (Unfavourable) barrier to formal access.
